newsitem.title: USA: Chesapeake Energy active in Austin Chalk.
newsitem.headline: Chesapeake Energy active in Austin Chalk.

text.p: Chesapeake Energy Corp said it has participated in 10 of the 17 successful wells in the deepest part of the Louisiana Austin Chalk trend.

Pointing out the industry continues to accelerate drilling activities in the Louisiana Trend, it said operations have commenced on 19 additional wells in the deeper part of the trend where Chesapeake has concentrated its operations with the company participating in 10.
It also noted there have been five dry holes of which Chesapeake has drilled three.

To date in January, the company said, it is receiving about $4.O0 per thousand cubic feet and $26.00 per barrel of oil for its Austin Chalk production in Louisiana, generating operating cash flow of approximately $4.00 per Mcfe, after lifting and general and administrative costs.

The continuous use of 10 rigs during 1997 would enable Chesapeake to begin drilling operations on about 35 Louisiana Trend wells, the company noted, adding it has scheduled three to target the Tuscaloosa formation.
In the Masters Creek area, Chesapeake said, it started oil and natural gas sales from the Martin 11 1 in December.

During its first month of production, the well averaged 1,200 barrels of oil and 4.6 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from a single Austin Chalk lateral. Chesapeake owns a 78 percent working interest in the Martin, with Occidental Petroleum Corp's OXY USA Inc and several private parties owning the remaining working interest.

Also in Masters Creek, Chesapeake recently started oil and natural gas sales from the Lawton 31 1. During its first two weeks of production, the well averaged 3,650 barresl of oil and 10.2 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from a single Austin Chalk lateral.

Chesapeake owns a 75 percent working interest in the Lawton 31, with Union Pacific Resources Group Inc, OXY USA, Helmerich & Payne Inc and several private parties owning the remaining working interest.

Chesapeake's first Tuscaloosa producer, the Thomas 40 1, began producing on December 30. During its first ten days of production, this vertical well averaged 1,050 barrels of oil and 4.3 million cubic feet of natural gas daily. Chesapeake owns a 63 percent working interest in the Thomas, with several private parties owning the remaining working interest.
As a result of the success of the Thomas, the company has started drilling the Zachary 98 1, as a one mile west offset.
Chesapeake said it is drilling with ten rigs to continue developing its deep Giddings leasehold, where two wells were completed early this month.

Completed on January 1, the Hermann 1-H averaged 48.1 million cubic feet per day during its first week of production from a single Austin Chalk lateral. Chesapeake owns a 53 percent working interest in the Hermann, with Belco Oil & Gas Corp and several private parties owning the rest.
The company said it plans to drill three other wells in the immediate vicinity during the next few months.

Completed on January 4, the Quarry 1-H averaged 23.2 million cubic feet daily during its first four days of production from a single Austin Chalk lateral. Chesapeake owns a 69 percent working interest in the Quarry, with Belco and several private investors owning the rest.
The company will soon begin two offsets to the Quarry.
In the Knox, Golden Trend, and Sholem Alechem fields of southern Oklahoma, Chesapeake is using nine rigs to further develop its large inventory of undrilled locations, it said.

In the Red River play of North Dakota and Montana, Chesapeake's first two vertical wells have been successful while its first horizontal well was non-productive. The company said it will continue drilling with one or two rigs during the next few months.

In the Lovington oil project in the Lea County, N.M., portion of the Permian Basin, Chesapeake has successfully completed its first four Strawn formation tests. In these four wells, the company owns an average of 75 percent working interest, with several private parties owning the remaining working interest.
Chesapeake believes up to 50 prospective vertical wells can be drilled on its Lovington leasehold and it expects to drill 10 to 20 of these prospects during 1997.
Chesapeake plans to announce its second quarter fiscal 1997 earnings on January 23, it added.
((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
